title: Apply sealed next-vote Signal Jam and one-round Grid Failure
prompt: Read README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/SWARM_PILOT.md, docs/PILOT100_BACKLOG.md and the frozen sources under docs/design/ first. RULES-SPEC-v1.md is the canonical six-node deterministic gameplay contract; completed foundation APIs remain compatibility history. Implement new versioned APIs without changing the completed T01–T10 contracts. Work only in declared ownership; no manifests, shared exports or dependencies unless explicitly owned. Engine production remains ES2022-only, pure and independent from Firebase, Node, browser, UI and Capacitor. Use original synthetic test data and injected authority time/entropy; no clocks or global randomness in engine. Never expose seed, roles, private inputs or raw audit data through public output. Do not invent a rule where an explicit design gap is named. Run scoped lint/typecheck/tests and npm run check; report contract changes and observed results. No commits, pushes, PRs, child agents, cloud deployment, credentials or budget changes. At S2 mark the next Crew vote sealed: targets stay hidden until deadline/resolution instead of card animations revealing them. Consume the seal for exactly that next vote, not forever. At S3 current Shift Lead targets one other active player for next-round Jam; apply Safeguard before effect, validate authority/revision and use the same one-round eligibility machinery. Emit track.sabotage.signal_jam/grid_failure and persistent status descriptors without private alignments.
acceptance: A sealed vote hides chosen candidate mappings from every public/other-recipient surface until the correct resolution boundary.
S3 cannot target current Shift Lead or an inactive spectator and Jam blocks the exact next-round vote/Crew window.
Safeguard consumes instead of applying Jam; duplicate/replayed powers cannot extend status or reuse the one granted action.
Scoped lint, typecheck and tests plus npm run check pass; legacy APIs retain compatibility and only owned files change.
